### Helper Functions

```{r theme-helper}
theme_thesis <- function(base_size = 10) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = base_size + 4),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = base_size - 1, colour = "grey40"),
      plot.caption  = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = base_size - 3, colour = "grey50"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = base_size - 1),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}

theme_thesis_map <- function(base_size = 10) {
  theme_void(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, size = base_size + 4),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = base_size - 1, colour = "grey40"),
      plot.caption  = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = base_size - 3, colour = "grey50"),
      legend.title = element_text(size = base_size - 1),
      legend.position = "right"
    )
}
```

```{r save-helper}
save_figure <- function(plot, filename, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 300) {
  if (!dir.exists("figures")) dir.create("figures")
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file.path("figures", filename),
    plot     = plot,
    width    = width,
    height   = height,
    dpi      = dpi,
    bg       = "white"
  )
  
  cat("Saved:", file.path("figures", filename), "\n")
}
```

```{r model-helpers}
# Spatial models
extract_spatial_model <- function(model, label) {
  s <- summary(model)
  coefs <- as.data.frame(s$Coef)
  coefs$term <- rownames(coefs)
  n_obs <- length(residuals(model)) 

  coefs |>
    rename(estimate = Estimate, std_error = `Std. Error`, p_value = `Pr(>|z|)`) |>
    mutate(
      model       = label,
      n           = n_obs,
      significant = p_value < 0.05
    ) |>
    select(model, n, term, estimate, std_error, p_value, significant)
}

# Linear models
extract_model <- function(model, label) {
  r2 <- broom::glance(model)$adj.r.squared 

  broom::tidy(model) |>
    filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
    mutate(
      model       = label,
      r_squared   = r2,
      significant = p.value < 0.05
    ) |>
    select(model, term, estimate, p.value, significant, r_squared)
}

# Residuals vs Fitted, Scale-Location, and Cook's D plots for an lm() object
diagnose_lm <- function(model, label = deparse(substitute(model))) {
  df <- broom::augment(model)

  p1 <- ggplot(df, aes(.fitted, .resid)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
    labs(title = paste("Residuals vs Fitted:", label))

  p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(.fitted, sqrt(abs(.std.resid)))) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
    geom_smooth(method = "loess", colour = "black", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.6) +
    labs(title = paste("Scale-Location:", label), y = expression(sqrt("|Standardized residuals|")))

  cooks_d <- cooks.distance(model)
  p3 <- tibble(cooks_d = cooks_d) |>
    arrange(desc(cooks_d)) |>
    mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
    slice_head(n = 50) |>
    ggplot(aes(rank, cooks_d)) +
    geom_point() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 4 / length(cooks_d), colour = "red", linetype = "dashed") +
    labs(title = paste("Top 50 Cook's Distance:", label), subtitle = "Red line = 4/n threshold")

  print(p1); print(p2); print(p3)
  cat(label, "- points exceeding 4/n Cook's D threshold:", sum(cooks_d > 4 / length(cooks_d)), "\n")

  invisible(cooks_d)
}
```

```{r knn-helper}
# KNN spatial weights from a coordinate matrix
knn_listw <- function(coords, k) {
  nb2listw(knn2nb(knearneigh(coords, k = k)), style = "W", zero.policy = TRUE)
}

# Fit one spatial model at a given k and return its fit statistics. Used to
# scan several k values when choosing a KNN neighbourhood size (07_robustness.qmd).
scan_k <- function(k, coords, data, formula, fit_fun = sacsarlm) {
  listw <- knn_listw(coords, k)
  model <- fit_fun(formula, data = data, listw = listw, zero.policy = TRUE)
  moran <- moran.test(residuals(model), listw, zero.policy = TRUE)
  tibble(
    k       = k,
    AIC     = AIC(model),
    rho     = model$rho,
    lambda  = if (!is.null(model$lambda)) model$lambda else NA_real_,
    moran_i = moran$estimate[["Moran I statistic"]],
    moran_p = moran$p.value
  )
}
```
